PAST PERFORMANCE: A list of contracts within the last three (3) years for the provision of comparable biometric or large database identity management systems to federal or commercial customers. The list shall include contact information (name, organization, email, and phone) and be limited to no more than five (5) references. CERTIFICATIONS: Certified knowledge of the company that will provide installation and support expertise, including direct OEM engineering qualifications. REFERENCES: Companies/Agencies that have received similar biometric equipment and integration services from the vendor. CONTRACT TITLE: Subscription for EP Evaluator Software This procurement is for commercial subscription services supporting the continued use of a software platform by the Pathology and Laboratory Medicine Service (PLMS) at the Jonathan M. Wainwright Memorial VA Medical Center (VAWW). The subscription shall provide uninterrupted access to the software application and associated manufacturer-supported services necessary to perform analytical verification, method validation, instrument comparison, reportable range verification, reference interval verification, precision studies, linearity studies, interference studies, and other statistical analyses required to support clinical laboratory operations. Subscription services shall include software licensing, manufacturer-provided maintenance, software updates, version upgrades, technical support, and access to product documentation and training resources throughout the period of performance. The requested subscription services support compliance with applicable Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments (CLIA), College of American Pathologists (CAP), Veterans Health Administration (VHA), and Clinical and Laboratory Standards In

ents new instrumentation, introduces new testing methodologies, modifies existing assays, and performs verification studies necessary to ensure the accuracy, precision, and clinical reliability of patient testing. Federal regulations, accreditation standards, and VHA policy require laboratories to perform analytical verification and validation studies before implementing new instrumentation, new methodologies, or significant modifications to existing testing systems. These studies routinely include, but are not limited to, precision, method comparison, analytical measurement range (AMR), reportable range, linearity, calibration verification, reference interval verification, interference, carryover, and other analytical performance evaluations necessary to demonstrate that laboratory testing systems perform as intended. Documentation supporting these activities must be maintained and be suitable for review during inspections conducted under CLIA, CAP, and other applicable regulatory or accrediting organizations. Manual statistical analysis and documentation of analytical verification studies are labor-intensive, increase the potential for transcription and calculation errors, and may result in inconsistent documentation between laboratory sections or individual users. The Government requi

ecessary to maintain full subscription functionality. The contractor shall provide all subscription services required to support continued use of the software for analytical verification and validation studies performed in accordance with applicable CLIA, CAP, VHA, and CLSI requirements. The requested subscription services shall support the laboratory’s ongoing performance of analytical verification and validation studies, including implementation of new instrumentation, new analytical methods, assay modifications, method comparison studies, precision studies, analytical measurement range and reportable range verification, linearity studies, reference interval verification, interference studies, carryover evaluations, and other analytical performance assessments required to support clinical laboratory operations. The subscription shall provide uninterrupted access to previously created projects, historical validation studies, statistical analyses, and associated reports maintained within the software throughout the period of performance. Multiple sites have requested comprehensive instruction in Oversize and Ivotion Dentures using both 3Shape and CAM workflows, which requires approximately 2.5 to 3 days of training. Additional requested modules include Crown and Bridge, Screw Retained Crown and Bridge, and Custom Abutments. These validated workflows are necessary to maintain staff competency and meet ongoing clinical demand. Workflows related to implant-supported dentures and dentures over titanium bars have been excluded, as they are not currently validated. Purpose U.S. Central Command (USCENTCOM) Office of Legislative Affairs (LA) requires a secure, web-based subscription service that provides comprehensive, nonpartisan reporting, analysis, and alerts on U.S. Congressional activity, federal policy developments, and budget and appropriations matters relevant to USCENTCOM equities. The service shall enable LA personnel to monitor legislative and policy developments, support senior leader engagements, and prepare for Congressional hearings, testimony, and engagements with Members of Congress and sta

ropriations matters relevant to USCENTCOM equities. The service shall enable LA personnel to monitor legislative and policy developments, support senior leader engagements, and prepare for Congressional hearings, testimony, and engagements with Members of Congress and staff. 2. Scope The contractor shall provide an online platform that delivers timely, accurate, and nonpartisan coverage of: Congressional activity (hearings, markups, floor action) Defense policy and national security issues Federal budget and appropriations processes Executive branch policy developments U.S. policy affecting the CENTCOM Area of Responsibility (AOR) 3. General Requirements 3.1 User Access and Support Provide access for up to 6 licensed users Provide initial onboarding and training (virtual or telephonic) Provide ongoing customer support upon request 3.2 Search and Content Discovery The platform shall provide: A global search capability across all available content Ability to search using: Keywords Topics Policy areas Congressional activity Ability to quickly locate relevant reporting, analysis, and source-linked materials 3.3 Alerts and Notifications The platform shall provide customizable alerting capabilities, including: User-defined alerts based on: Keywords Policy topics Legislative activity Committees and

ports via email 3.8 Policy and Stakeholder Awareness The platform shall provide: Insight into policy positions, legislative priorities, and public statements of Members of Congress and executive branch officials Aggregated reporting incorporating: Public statements Press releases Relevant media and policy developments 3.9 Coverage of CENTCOM-Relevant Issues The platform shall provide reporting and analysis related to: U.S. policy affecting the CENTCOM Area of Responsibility Defense posture, operations, and authorities relevant to USCENTCOM Congressional actions impacting regional security, partner nations, and military operations 4. Security Requirements The platform shall be password-protected Access shall be restricted to authorized users only 5. Performance Requirements Content shall be updated on a continuous basis as developments occur Alerts and newsletters shall be delivered in a timely manner consistent with industry standards 6. Deliverables The contractor shall provide: Platform access for authorized users Ongoing reporting, analysis, and alerts Customer support and training services 7. This procurement supports the Clement J. Zablocki VA Medical Center, Stereotactic Radiosurgery (SRS) Program, located at 5000 W. National Avenue, Milwaukee, WI 53295. This notice of intent is not a request for competitive proposals. No solicitation document is available, and no request for quotes will be issued. The Government requires the isoPoint™ Isocenter Characterization System, a proprietary optical tracking and 3D mechanical isocenter analysis solution used for precision quality assurance of stereotactic radiosurgery operations. The system consists of: Stereo-camera pod Tracking modules Precision mechanical markers Software capable of 3D characterization, mechanical axis assessment, collimator and couch analysis, and beam-to-target error computation The isoPoint™ system will enhance the accuracy and efficiency of quality assurance for the facility’s Elekta Versa HD LINAC, providing real-time 3D mechanical data not achievable through existing Winston–Lutz methodologies. The system’s capability to achieve sub-0.01 mm mechanical precision is critical to maintaining clinical standards for the SRS program. Aktina Medical is the so

The isoPoint™ is the only known system capable of conducting direct mechanical rotational axis measurements of LINAC subsystems and generating a full 3D error matrix. Other QA tools rely on image-based estimation and lack the ability to perform subsystem-specific mechanical characterization. Only Aktina Medical’s isoPoint™ system meets the clinical, technical, and operational requirements necessary to safely support the facility’s stereotactic radiosurgery program. entity_geography.text: VA Campus requires significant improvements, as it does not provide the coverage, reliability, or capability necessary to support modern security operations across a campus of this size and population density. Identified deficiencies including gaps in camera coverage, aging or degraded equipment, limited real-time monitoring capability, and the absence of intelligent analytics constrain OSLE's ability to detect, deter, and respond to security incidents in a timely manner and place an unsustainable burden on personnel who must manually monitor a large volume of camera feeds. Addressing these deficiencies is essential to protecting the growing resident population at NCWI and maintaining a secure environment across the West Los Angeles VA Campus. In support of enhanced security operations, the VA intends to incorporate Artificial Intelligence (AI) capabilities to assist in reviewing surveillance footage, enabling the rapid identification of weapons that are in plain view and not concealed. AI-based detection is intended to augment not replace, the vigilance of VA Police and security personnel by continuously analyzing video feeds, flagging visible weapons in real time, and accelerating the delivery of actionable alerts to responders. deliverables_scope.text: ==== FILE: files/36C10B26Q0746.docx ===== GENERAL INFORMATION PLACE OF PERFORMANCE ADDITIONAL INFORMATION DESCRIPTION Introduction This Request for Information (RFI) is issued for information and planning purposes only and does not constitute a solicitation nor does it restrict the Government as to the ultimate acquisition approach. In accordance with Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation Overhaul (RFO) 15.101(c), responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. The purpose of this RFI is to identify qualified vendors, who are able to meet Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) requirements for Greater Los Angeles Artificial Intelligence Threat Detection. Any contract/order that might be awarded based on information received or derived from this market research will be the outcome of the competitive process. The purpose of this RFI is to obtain market information on capable sources of supply, industry’s best practices, and input specifically the information provided. The Government is not responsible for any cost incurred by industry in furnishing this information. All costs associated with responding to this RFI will be solely at the interested vendor's expense. Not responding to this RFI does not preclude participation in any

ies, OSLE has determined that the existing video surveillance system at the West Los Angeles VA Campus requires significant improvements, as it does not provide the coverage, reliability, or capability necessary to support modern security operations across a campus of this size and population density. Identified deficiencies including gaps in camera coverage, aging or degraded equipment, limited real-time monitoring capability, and the absence of intelligent analytics constrain OSLE's ability to detect, deter, and respond to security incidents in a timely manner and place an unsustainable burden on personnel who must manually monitor a large volume of camera feeds. Addressing these deficiencies is essential to protecting the growing resident population at NCWI and maintaining a secure environment across the West Los Angeles VA Campus. In support of enhanced security operations, the VA intends to incorporate Artificial Intelligence (AI) capabilities to assist in reviewing surveillance footage, enabling the rapid identification of weapons that are in plain view and not concealed. AI-based detection is intended to augment not replace, the vigilance of VA Police and security personnel by continuously analyzing video feeds, flagging visible weapons in real time, and accelerating the deliver

This portfolio supports a wide range of stakeholders, including OPNAV N95, PMW 130, PMW 150, PMW 160, PMW 170, PMW 770, PMW 790, PMS 406, PMS 408, PMS 420, PMS 385, PMS 485, PMS 495, USFFC-NECC, USFFC-NSW, NCIS, PAE Mission Systems, PAE Maritime, PEO Ships, Amphibious Assault and Connectors Program, PEO Digital, Office of Naval Research (ONR) Transportation Security Administration (TSA), Air Force, Army, Coast Guard, and Marine

Transportation Security Administration (TSA), Air Force, Army, Coast Guard, and Marine Corps. The complexity and persistent evolution of modern cyber threats necessitate specialized technical expertise to supplement the existing government workforce. The operational landscape demands a strategic evolution beyond traditional, static compliance models toward a dynamic, threat-informed, and resilient Cyber Ready posture. This forward-leaning approach is essential to guaranteeing the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of all designated Department of Defense (DoD) information systems, networks, and data, thereby ensuring mission assurance in the face of sophisticated adversaries. This Performance Work Statement (PWS) outlines the expert contractor support required to meet these critical defense objectives. The Contractor shall provide all qualified personnel, supervision, and services required to execute a comprehensive, full-lifecycle cybersecurity program. This effort encompasses all C5ISRT systems, networks, applications, and data across all operating environments, including on-premises data centers, cloud platforms, and the tactical edge. The scope requires a proactive "secure-by-design" philosophy, focusing on operational risk management, cyber survivability, an

ional risk management, cyber survivability, and the seamless integration of security into all phases of the system lifecycle. The services to be performed include, but are not limited to, strategic advisory, policy and risk analysis, security engineering and architecture, threat intelligence, advanced vulnerability management, proactive security operations, compliance auditing, and workforce training. This program supports a wide range of critical systems and initiatives executed for NSWC PCD as well as for the key stakeholders mentioned above. The work is organized into the following principal performance areas:  Cybersecurity Assurance and Risk Management: Providing expert support for all Assessment and Authorization (A&A) functions and sustaining a risk management program aligned with the Risk Management Framework (RMF) and the strategic principles of the Cybersecurity Risk Management Construct (CSRMC). A primary focus is the execution of all RMF steps with the strategic goal of achieving and maintaining a state of Continuous Authority to Operate (cATO). This includes developing and maintaining all authorization artifacts (e.g., SSP, SAP, SAR, POA&M), managing the system portfolio within eMASS, and providing expert guidance on control implementation, reciprocity, an

The IHS is the principal Federal health care provider and health advocate for Indian people, and its goal is to raise their health status to the highest possible level. The IHS provides a comprehensive health service delivery system for approximately 2.6 million American Indians and Alaska Natives who belong to 574 Federally recognized tribes in 37 states.
